correctness.rationale: Exact row-payoff equations \(U_C=d(b-2c)+mc\), \(U_D=mb\), and \(U_I=d(b-c_I)\) reconstruct the source matrix for degrees one and two. The strict local best replies are \(I\) at zero cooperative neighbors, \(D\) at two, and \(C\) at one for degree two precisely when \(b>3c\) and \(c_I>3c/2\); degree-one replies are \(I\) then \(D\). Cooperative components are therefore isolated \(CC\) dimers bracketed by defectors, forcing three-periodicity and different path/cycle closure conditions. Exact-rational exhaustive comparisons passed 85 graph/parameter cases. Computation verifies finite cases only; the analytic proof covers all finite orders.

value.rationale: A complete necessary-and-sufficient equilibrium classification for all maximum-degree-two networks is structurally motivated by the 2026 paper’s degree-two finite-size ring experiments. The source uses a 10000-agent ring with rare mutations, yet the theorem shows no cooperative pure Nash equilibrium is possible there, although a 9999-agent ring has exactly three in the same payoff regime. This separates finite noisy coexistence from pure Nash recurrence and quantifies a sharp graph-boundary effect. This is not marketed as a new local payoff threshold or a stochastic-ergodic result.
